generatedCommentsNodes.comment: The change from `EsIndex` to `String indexName` and `Map<String, IndexMode> indexNameWithModes` in multiple classes like `EsRelation`, `EsQueryExec`, and `EsSourceExec` requires careful verification of all usages. Ensure that the transition does not introduce any null pointer exceptions or incorrect handling of indices.

The method `indexNameWithModes()` should be consistently used wherever the index modes are required. Ensure that all places where `index().indexNameWithModes()` was previously used now correctly use `indexNameWithModes()`.
The `indexName` field should be validated to ensure it is not null or empty. This validation should be added in the constructors of classes like `EsRelation`, `EsQueryExec`, and `EsSourceExec`.
The `indexNameWithModes` map should be included in the `nodeString` method to provide a complete string representation of the object.
The `indexNameWithModes` map should be serialized and deserialized correctly. Ensure that the serialization logic in methods like `writeTo` and `readFrom` handles the map properly.
The `indexNameWithModes` map should be included in the hash code and equals methods to ensure proper comparison of objects.
The `indexNameWithModes` field should be validated to ensure it is not null. This validation should be added in the constructors of classes like `EsRelation`, `EsQueryExec`, and `EsSourceExec`.

The changes in test cases for serialization size (e.g., `ByteSizeValue.ofBytes`) should be verified against the actual expected sizes after the removal of `EsIndex` mapping serialization. Ensure that these values are accurate and reflect the current state.
Ensure that the `indexNameWithModes` map is immutable or properly synchronized if it is shared across threads. This will prevent concurrent modification issues.

review_comment:
If this is the only thing that requires that: I believe this check could happen much earlier. Potentially already in the analyzer on the coordinator node. We shouldn't need to wait until the local planning to determine that an index isn't a lookup index.

Could you maybe check if it's feasible to move that to an earlier place and, thus, remove the `indexNameWithModes` map altogether from the `EsRelation` and related classes?

Happy to assist with moving that to an earlier stage!

There already is an index mode check in the Analyzer: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/4ac8d55ff7c5612413e4a45e14a2b39f3e85f3a9/x-pack/plugin/esql/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/esql/analysis/Analyzer.java#L239-L255

I think I got it. The check is indeed already performed and could be removed - it's just there out of defensiveness as far as I can see.

What cannot be removed is the line
```
 var entry = indicesWithModes.entrySet().iterator().next(); 
```
which, in case of aliases, contains the _actual_ lookup index name in the entry's key.

Looks to me like we should add a comment and leave this as-is. (Well, and maybe remove the defensive double validation, but it also doesn't hurt.)

I'll confirm with @idegtiarenko if this is what we want to do.
Correct. IndexName could actually be alias or pattern, while map entries include resolved index names
@costin , we decided removing this map is too large in scope for this PR. Ievgen opened a follow-up issue: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/120210

The map seems similar to EsIndex - it's detailed information that isn't required.
Nit: doing it in a separate PR will require a transport bump; maybe consider this complete but not merge, do the follow-up PR and then merge them at the same time to have only one increment?

I am not sure I would be able to pick up followup immediately.
Also keeping this updated required multiple conflict resolutions. 
I would really prefer to merge this earlier.
This test file beautifully demonstrates the improvements from the change. Awesome, in this particularly bad case we got a reduction by 99.996%!
